source_receipts.location: Abstract and Results: associations of prevalence, shedding, susceptibility, and persistence in replicate host populations.
source_receipts.finding: The primary study makes a bounded association claim and reports measured strain, line, and block effects that remain partly unexplained.

source_receipts.location: spill.char.dataset1.csv and Strainsandblocks.csv, verified MD5 receipts.
source_receipts.finding: The official record retains per-line epidemiological characteristics, persistence outcomes, host strain, and experimental-block membership.
The published correlative workflow fits pooled models with random block and strain effects, then visualizes fitted relationships; it does not show a held-block predictive assessment.

question: Do the reported early-characteristic associations predict persistence in a predeclared experimental block held out from fitting, rather than only describing the pooled blocks?
fragility: A pooled association with a random block effect can describe the observed blocks without demonstrating transfer to a new block.
alternative_explanation: The reported relationship may be driven by block-specific handling, strain composition, or an unmeasured line effect rather than a transportable early-epidemiology signal.
independent_check: Predeclare predictor set, scale, and outcome; fit the published correlative model on all but one experimental block, predict the held block, rotate across blocks, and compare predictive calibration with the pooled fit without changing the biological measurements.

outcomes.positive: Consistent held-block calibration supports the narrow transportability of the early-characteristic association.
outcomes.null: Weak or imprecise held-block prediction means the data support pooled association but not established block transfer.
outcomes.contrary: Systematic held-block failure challenges the claimed predictive scope and requires virology/statistical review before biological reinterpretation.

material_mismatch: The blocks are laboratory nematode-virus experiments, while the paper motivates spillover risk more broadly; a successful result would validate only block-level transfer within this system.
plain_language_verdict: INTERVIEW-READY CANDIDATE — the packet asks a bounded reproducibility question about transfer across experimental blocks. It neither predicts real-world outbreaks nor establishes a universal cross-domain pattern. It remains outside System 2 and outside target selection until an exactly-three-packet trio passes the first-interview gates.
next_permitted_action: Retain this second packet. Construct one contrasting packet, then apply the exactly-three-target first-interview gauntlet without selecting by apparent promise.
